issue.title: First-startup disk check ignores the chainstate
issue.body:
On first startup, `init.cpp` [warns](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4ef7904c39fa2c9eedc66d1a75caaf34c0c531b9/src/init.cpp#L2075) when free disk space may not fit the block files. The check never counts the chainstate (`AssumedChainStateSize()`), which seems incomplete, at least for pruned nodes, where the chainstate can dominate disk usage depending on the pruning configuration. For unpruned nodes it matters less, since the block files dominate, and the [release process](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4ef7904c39fa2c9eedc66d1a75caaf34c0c531b9/doc/release-process.md?plain=1#L330) says `m_assumed_blockchain_size` doesn't need to exclude the chainstate.

To address this fully, the check also has to handle a datadir and blocks dir on separate volumes. In that case each volume needs its own check, which means detecting whether two paths share a volume. That takes a new platform-specific helper.

I've tried to address these in: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...stringintech:bitcoin:refs/heads/2026/11/init-warn-chainstate-size

Counting the chainstate also affects the functional tests. Tests on non-regtest chains can hit this warning depending on the free space of the machine running them, and they work around it in different ways: [some](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4ef7904c39fa2c9eedc66d1a75caaf34c0c531b9/test/functional/feature_config_args.py#L26) pass `-prune` just to keep the estimate small, and [some](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/4ef7904c39fa2c9eedc66d1a75caaf34c0c531b9/test/functional/mining_mainnet.py#L79) truncate stderr. With the chainstate counted, the `-prune` workaround no longer avoids the warning unless the host has enough free space for the chainstate. Rather than that, the above branch takes a more direct approach and handles it with a test framework flag that drops the warning before stderr is checked when a node stops.

IMO a full fix is worth having. However, given that this warning is non-blocking, I'd like to hear whether others think the added complexity is justified, or see a different way to address this.
